LC oscillators rely on resonant frequency \( f = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}} \).  
For very high frequencies (GHz range), parasitic capacitances and inductances dominate, making LC oscillators impractical beyond roughly 500 MHz; at such high frequencies, crystal oscillators or transmission-line-based oscillators are preferred.  
At very low frequencies (kHz range), the required L and C values become impractically large (e.g., huge inductors), so RC oscillators or other types are used instead.  

Thus, LC oscillators are typically used from roughly 100 kHz to 500 MHz.  

Option (A) excludes lower frequencies where LC oscillators still work.  
Option (C) is too low in upper limit.  
Option (D) is far too high in upper limit.  
Option (B) matches the typical usable range.  

Final answer: (B)
